public.title: All Settlements
public.description: Each task is {delay,status,value}, where status is fulfilled or rejected. Return settlements in original task order, each as {status,value}; delay affects completion order but never output order. Delays are integers 0 through 1000. This deterministic adapter models aggregate settlement without real asynchronous callbacks. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Settlement order and aggregate output order are different.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Project each input task to its settlement record without sorting by delay. O(n) time and O(n) output space, plus retained value sizes. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
